biography.plain_text: Mohamed M. Abou El Enein is an Egyptian industrialist, diversified-group founder and parliamentarian. He moved from regional trade into ceramics manufacturing, opening his first factory in 1983 and building an export business serving more than 100 countries. Born in Cairo in 1951, he later combined business leadership with long-running parliamentary service.

long_biography.plain_text:
Abou El Enein began in trade after graduating from Helwan University. He first linked European suppliers with the Libyan market and later imported Italian ceramics into Egypt. In the late 1970s, he chose manufacturing, secured a factory licence and partnered with Italian machinery producer SACMI. Three-year bank financing helped him open the plant in 1983 with four production lines.

His businesses later expanded into porcelain, sanitary ware, agriculture, hotels, property, media, technology and aviation. Abou El Enein also built a long public career. He served as a national legislator for more than fifteen years and became deputy speaker during the last parliamentary term. He then won re-election and became president of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Union for the Mediterranean in 2025.
